case_126.label_scope: One fixed implementation over all finite FP16 scalar values and the complete public tensor contract; inputs only provide witnesses.
case_126.analysis: Every finite FP16 encoding is compared against a directed-rounding mathematical erf interval in multiple orders and storage alignments. Other lengths, tails, input preservation, backing guards and fresh storage are checked separately. Scalar enumeration does not by itself prove every shape specialization or compiler/memory behavior.

oracle.method: 320-bit MPFR erf under RoundDown and RoundUp, then outward binary64 endpoint conversion; 110-decimal mpmath erf crosschecks every nonnegative finite FP16 value; exact odd symmetry supplies negative bounds. No tail approximation is used.
oracle.scope: The directed-rounding interval is the numerical oracle. Independent mpmath agreement is a cross-check, not the source of the enclosure guarantee. Exhausting scalar FP16 encodings does not alone prove arbitrary tensor indexing, shape specialization, input preservation or fresh-output behavior.

indexing.argument: For the source index=program_id*256+lane, consecutive blocks cover adjacent disjoint integer intervals. For every legal N, the last block has 1..256 active lanes; mask index<N leaves exactly [0,N) once. All index arithmetic fits int32. Each lane reads one FP16 value and writes one independent FP32 output; N affects the mask, not scalar arithmetic.
indexing.scope: Exhaustive N check of the source indexing model plus its interval-partition argument. It is not an exhaustive GPU execution over every N, lane placement, address, or compiler specialization.

cpu_audit.scope: Exhaustive scalar input/reference validation; candidate GPU arithmetic and tensor properties are checked separately.
